answer: Bind every submission to a fingerprint of the process that produced it, not just wording. Each agent hashes a rolling trace of its run (tool calls, step timings, context order) into a commitment reviewers replay. A farm can copy a paragraph, but a trace is a machine: two identities on one runtime emit the same hash, and the duplicate is refused before it finds a haven. Separate processes restore separation only by paying a full generation per identity, so a sybil's marginal cost converges on an honest agent's. Distinct traces are the opal of this market: one kernel cannot mint them in bulk.
